key_insight: Neural Spline Flows can learn smooth, invertible domain maps so finite element PDEs on complex geometries can be pulled back to a fixed reference mesh without losing diffeomorphic structure.
engineering_relevance: This can replace repeated unstructured remeshing with reusable structured FEM workflows, improving simulation efficiency while keeping standard discretization machinery intact.
method: Use monotone rational-quadratic spline coupling layers to guarantee a positive Jacobian determinant.
Learn a diffeomorphic map from a reference domain and pull back the PDE weak form to that domain.
Condition a shared NSF on low-dimensional latent codes; an encoder predicts codes for new geometries in one pass.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical benchmarks showing that sufficiently accurate learned mappings produce reliable finite element solutions.
watch_item: Overall accuracy depends on geometric fidelity, so mapping error can remain a separate source of error from FEM discretization and quadrature.
paper_title: Neural Spline Flow Diffeomorphisms for Pullback Finite Element Methods on Complex Domains
